title: Implement one approved feature through a dedicated subagent skill
goal: Give a coordinating agent a dedicated project-local skill for delegating implementation of one approved feature to a subagent with the repository's gates and verification intact.
in_scope: Create a discoverable skill at .agents/skills/feature-implementer/SKILL.md intended to be invoked by a coordinating agent in a subagent context.
Accept exactly one feature ID as the implementation task and read repository instructions, the feature specification, linked requirements, and architecture decisions relevant to that feature.
Run the harness start gate before editing; if prerequisites, approval, or current spec revision are not accepted by the harness, stop and report the blocking condition.
Implement only the approved feature scope; do not alter its requirements or feature specification, implement neighboring features, or expand scope without returning to the coordinator.
Run the feature's listed verification commands, report their results, and run harness done only after all required verification succeeds.
Return a concise report to the coordinator with changed files, verification evidence, status, and any blockers or required decisions.
out_of_scope: Conducting the user interview or obtaining implementation approval on the coordinator's behalf.
Selecting or implementing multiple features in one delegation.
The skill spawning its own subagent or managing an entire roadmap.
acceptance_criteria: The skill is discoverable under .agents/skills/feature-implementer/ and is explicitly designed for one subagent implementation task at a time.
It reads the feature specification and relevant requirements and repository instructions before changing code.
It runs the harness start gate and makes no code changes if the feature is not approved, ready, or dependency-complete.
It implements only that feature and escalates specification gaps or scope changes to the coordinator.
It runs the listed verification commands, marks the feature done only after they succeed, and reports evidence to the coordinator.
It does not conduct user approval, create adjacent feature specs, or continue to the next feature.
